findings.title: Paginated subgroup lookups still NPE if the cached group is gone
findings.body: The null check added in getSubGroupsCount was not applied to the other delegate lookups in the same adapter. getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268 all do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. modelSupplier loads the persistence delegate and returns null when the DB row is already gone while this session still holds the cached GroupAdapter — the same cross-request race as the reported NPE. Those overloads are what paginated/search subgroup listing uses. A cache hit followed by a concurrent delete still throws NullPointerException and fails the request with HTTP 500. A missing delegate should yield an empty stream (and the stale cache entry should be invalidated) instead of being dereferenced.

findings.title: Concurrent regression test can pass without observing the race and leaks its reader
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a background thread that lists groups while the test thread deletes them, then sets deletedAll and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. The reader is never gated by a latch and is never joined, so the assertion can run before any list call has started, and it always runs before the in-flight list that overlaps the last deletes has finished. A server NPE from that call is recorded only after the assertion has already passed, so a green run does not show the concurrent getSubGroupsCount failure is fixed. If a delete throws, deletedAll stays false and the non-daemon reader loops forever, still calling managedRealm.admin() during later tests and blocking JVM shutdown. That same admin client is used concurrently by the deleter; it is not safe to share across threads, so the test can also fail on unrelated client errors or corrupt the client for subsequent tests.
